To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the expression levels of GRP78 and peroxiredexin 4 were increased over two folds with NaBu treatment while the expression level of pyruvate dehydrogenase E1 component subunit beta was decreased over two folds with the same treatment, as determined by MALDI-MS and MS-MS analyses, and that Western blot analyses confirmed the MS results for GRP78, ERp57 and HSC70, but the degree of change in protein expression level differed between Western

the proteomic analysis of NaBu-treated CHO cells showed that NaBu increased the expression level of GRP 78 (a chaperone) and decreased the expression level of PPH (an isomerase) while the expression levels of HSC70 and Epr57 (other chaperones) did not change.
the expression level of GRP 78, HSC 70 and ERp 57 was increased over two fold in CHO cells expressing human thromboietin with NaBu treatment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of proteins whose expression levels change with NaBu treatment in CHO cells producing thrombopoietins.
the identification of the intracellular responses to NaBu treatment and provides information for further studies of the mechanisms of NaBu action in mammalian cells.
the proteomic responses of NaBu treated cells, and provides a basis for the further study of the intracellular responses to NaBu treatment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of GRP 78, HSC 70, ERp57 and phosphopyruvates hydratase were increased and decreased by NaBu, respectively.
2-DE is a useful tool to identify proteins that are differentially expressed in cells with NaBu treatment, but that the expression level change determined by MS analysis may be overestimated.
2-DE and MALDI-TO-F/MS/MS are useful for identifying proteins and determining their relative expression levels, but that the results should be confirmed using a validating method.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

NaBu treatment of thrombopoetin producing CHO cells results in a change of protein expression levels for 28 proteins, and that these proteins are related to protein folding, protein transport and energy metabolism.

the use of 2-DE is a useful tool for comparative analysis of protein expression levels, however, it should be used with caution when the results are to be used to make conclusions regarding protein expression levels.
the proteomic profiles for NaBu treated cells are different from those for control cells and the expression level changes of GRP78 and HSC70 were validated by Western blot analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a 2-DED-based proteomic analysis of cells treated with NaBu is a useful method to understand the intracellular mechanisms of the NaBu-induced enhancement of human thrombopoetin expression.
2-DE is a powerful tool for the analysis of protein expression levels.
2-DE analysis of protein expression profiles of cells treated by NaBu can provide valuable information on the intracellular responses.
